#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
LOG=/tmp/gb10-setup.log
exec > >(tee -a "$LOG") 2>&1
echo "===== $(date) start ====="

echo '123456' | sudo -S -v
echo 'dell ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/99-night-desk >/dev/null
sudo chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/99-night-desk

cd /home/dell/nvidia-dell-hackathon

echo "===== pnpm install ====="
pnpm --dir apps/web install
echo "PNPM_OK"

echo "===== NemoClaw install / onboard ====="
export NEMOCLAW_PROVIDER=ollama
export NEMOCLAW_MODEL=nemotron-3.5-lightning
export NEMOCLAW_AGENT=openclaw
export NEMOCLAW_CONTEXT_WINDOW=32768
export NEMOCLAW_YES=1
export NEMOCLAW_ACCEPT_THIRD_PARTY_SOFTWARE=1
export NEMOCLAW_NON_INTERACTIVE=1
export NEMOCLAW_NO_EXPRESS=1
export NEMOCLAW_SANDBOX_NAME=night-desk
export NEMOCLAW_POLICY_MODE=suggested

if ! command -v nemoclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if [[ ! -s /tmp/nemoclaw.sh ]]; then
    curl -fsSL https://www.nvidia.com/nemoclaw.sh -o /tmp/nemoclaw.sh
  fi
  bash /tmp/nemoclaw.sh --non-interactive --yes-i-accept-third-party-software
else
  echo "nemoclaw already installed: $(command -v nemoclaw)"
fi

# ensure CLI is on PATH after install
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.nemoclaw/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
hash -r || true
if ! command -v nemoclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Looking for nemoclaw binary..."
  find "$HOME" /usr/local /opt -name nemoclaw -type f 2>/dev/null | head
fi

if [[ ! -f "$HOME/.nemoclaw/ollama-proxy-token" ]]; then
  echo "===== nemoclaw onboard ====="
  nemoclaw onboard --non-interactive --yes --yes-i-accept-third-party-software
else
  echo "proxy token already present"
fi

TOKEN=""
if [[ -f "$HOME/.nemoclaw/ollama-proxy-token" ]]; then
  TOKEN="$(tr -d '\n' < "$HOME/.nemoclaw/ollama-proxy-token")"
fi

if [[ -n "$TOKEN" ]]; then
  BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:11435/v1"
  API_KEY="$TOKEN"
else
  echo "WARN: NemoClaw proxy token missing, falling back to raw Ollama :11434"
  BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1"
  API_KEY="ollama"
fi

ENV_BODY=$(cat <<EOF
LLM_BASE_URL=${BASE_URL}
LLM_API_KEY=${API_KEY}
LLM_MODEL=nemotron-3.5-lightning
EMBEDDING_MODEL=nomic-embed-text
NEMOCLAW_CONTEXT_WINDOW=32768
EOF
)
printf '%s\n' "$ENV_BODY" > /home/dell/nvidia-dell-hackathon/.env
printf '%s\n' "$ENV_BODY" > /home/dell/nvidia-dell-hackathon/apps/web/.env.local
echo "ENV_WRITTEN base=$BASE_URL"

echo "===== copy deal-diligence skill ====="
SKILL_SRC=/home/dell/nvidia-dell-hackathon/openclaw/skills/deal-diligence
SKILL_DESTS=()
for d in \
  "$HOME/.openclaw/skills" \
  "$HOME/.openclaw/workspace/skills" \
  "$HOME/.nemoclaw/openclaw/skills" \
  "$HOME/.nemoclaw/workspace/skills"; do
  if [[ -d "$(dirname "$d")" ]] || [[ -d "$d" ]]; then
    SKILL_DESTS+=("$d")
  fi
done
# also search
while IFS= read -r p; do
  SKILL_DESTS+=("$p")
done < <(find "$HOME/.openclaw" "$HOME/.nemoclaw" "$HOME/.ollama" -type d -name skills 2>/dev/null | head -20)
if [[ ${#SKILL_DESTS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.openclaw/skills"
  SKILL_DESTS+=("$HOME/.openclaw/skills")
fi
for dest in "${SKILL_DESTS[@]}"; do
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  cp -R "$SKILL_SRC" "$dest/"
  echo "copied skill -> $dest/deal-diligence"
done

echo "===== sample files ====="
pnpm --dir apps/web exec tsx lib/diligence/cli.ts sample || true

echo "===== start next ====="
tmux has-session -t nightdesk 2>/dev/null && tmux kill-session -t nightdesk || true
tmux new-session -d -s nightdesk -c /home/dell/nvidia-dell-hackathon \
  "export PATH=\"\$HOME/.local/bin:\$PATH\"; pnpm --dir apps/web dev --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 3000"

echo "===== launch openclaw ====="
tmux has-session -t openclaw 2>/dev/null && tmux kill-session -t openclaw || true
tmux new-session -d -s openclaw \
  "export PATH=\"\$HOME/.local/bin:\$PATH\"; ollama launch openclaw --model nemotron-3.5-lightning -y"

echo "===== wait for :3000 ====="
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health >/tmp/health.json 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "HEALTH_OK"
    cat /tmp/health.json
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done

set -euo pipefail
echo 123456 | sudo -S -v
mkdir -p /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix
cd /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix
# 6.17 tree is close to this kernel
curl -fsSL -o cdc_ncm.c https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.17/drivers/net/usb/cdc_ncm.c
# confirm apple private + iPad entries exist
grep -n "12AB\|apple_private\|1905" cdc_ncm.c | head
# insert Mac IDs after iPad block
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("cdc_ncm.c")
s = p.read_text()
needle = """\t{ USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(0x05ac, 0x12ab, 4),
\t\t.driver_info = (unsigned long)&apple_private_interface_info,
\t},
"""
insert = needle + """
\t/* Mac */
\t{ USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(0x05ac, 0x1905, 0),
\t\t.driver_info = (unsigned long)&apple_private_interface_info,
\t},
\t{ USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(0x05ac, 0x1905, 2),
\t\t.driver_info = (unsigned long)&apple_private_interface_info,
\t},
"""
if "0x1905" in s:
    print("already patched")
elif needle not in s:
    raise SystemExit("needle not found")
else:
    p.write_text(s.replace(needle, insert, 1))
    print("patched")
PY
grep -n "1905\|12ab" cdc_ncm.c | head
cat > Makefile <<'EOF'
obj-m := cdc_ncm.o
EOF
make -C /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build M=$PWD modules
ls -l cdc_ncm.ko
REMOTE

# Mac ↔ Dell GB10 USB-C transfer

Wi-Fi rsync between the Mac and the Dell Pro Max sits at about **1–2 MB/s**. A USB-C cable is the fast path. Thunderbolt host-to-host will not come up: the Dell Type-C ports are **USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 (20 Gbps) + DP**, not Thunderbolt.

This is the log of what actually worked (2026-09-12).

## What you need

- USB-C cable, Mac → any Type-C port on the Dell
- SSH key already on the box (`~/.ssh/dell_gb10` on the Mac, user `dell`)
- Linux kernel headers on the box (`linux-headers-$(uname -r)`) so you can rebuild `cdc_ncm`

Addresses used here:

| Side | Interface | Address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dell | `enx52ff74300b99` | `169.254.67.1/16` |
| Mac | `en4` (Ethernet Adapter) | `169.254.50.165` (IPv4LL, automatic) |

Interface names on the Dell are derived from the NCM MAC. If they change after a replug, pick the `enx52ff…` iface that comes up with the cable and put `169.254.67.1/16` on that one.

SSH alias on the Mac (`~/.ssh/config`):

```
Host dell-usb
    HostName 169.254.67.1
    User dell
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/dell_gb10
    IdentitiesOnly yes
    Compression no

Host dell-gb10
    HostName 10.158.158.1
    User dell
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/dell_gb10
    IdentitiesOnly yes
```

## Why stock Linux does not bind

The Mac appears as USB device **`05ac:1905` “Apple Inc. Mac”**, CDC NCM, two functions (ifaces 0 and 2). There is **no interrupt status endpoint**.

Stock `cdc_ncm` already quirks iPhone/iPad (`05ac:12a8`, `05ac:12ab`) as `CDC NCM (Apple Private)`. It does **not** list Mac `1905`. Probe then fails:

```
cdc_ncm 3-1:1.0: bind() failure
cdc_ncm 3-1:1.2: bind() failure
```

`echo 05ac 1905 > /sys/bus/usb/drivers/cdc_ncm/new_id` is not enough. `new_id` attaches the generic NCM info (`FLAG_LINK_INTR`), which still requires the missing status endpoint.

The missing quirk is the same idea as [this linux-kernel patch](https://lists.openwall.net/linux-kernel/2026/04/29/1790): match `05ac:1905` ifaces 0 and 2 with `apple_private_interface_info`.

This box was `6.17.0-1031-nvidia`. That build had 12a8/12ab, not 1905.

## Patch and load `cdc_ncm` on the Dell

Run on the Dell (Wi-Fi SSH is fine for this step):

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix && cd /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix
curl -fsSL -o cdc_ncm.c https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.17/drivers/net/usb/cdc_ncm.c
```

Insert the Mac IDs immediately after the iPad (`0x12ab`) block:

```c
	/* Mac */
	{ USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(0x05ac, 0x1905, 0),
		.driver_info = (unsigned long)&apple_private_interface_info,
	},
	{ USB_DEVICE_INTERFACE_NUMBER(0x05ac, 0x1905, 2),
		.driver_info = (unsigned long)&apple_private_interface_info,
	},
```

Build and replace the in-tree module. `cdc_mbim` depends on `cdc_ncm`, so unload it first:

```bash
cat > Makefile <<'EOF'
obj-m := cdc_ncm.o
EOF
make -C /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build M=$PWD modules

sudo rmmod cdc_mbim || true
sudo rmmod cdc_ncm || true
sudo insmod /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix/cdc_ncm.ko
sudo modprobe cdc_mbim || true
```

Success looks like:

```
cdc_ncm 3-1:1.0 usb0: register 'cdc_ncm' at usb-NVDA8000:01-1, CDC NCM (Apple Private), …
cdc_ncm 3-1:1.2 usb1: register 'cdc_ncm' at usb-NVDA8000:01-1, CDC NCM (Apple Private), …
```

udev renames them to `enx52ff74300b99` and `enx52ff74300b79`. Use the first one (iface 0).

### Persist across reboot

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/updates
sudo cp /tmp/cdc_ncm_fix/cdc_ncm.ko /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/updates/cdc_ncm.ko
sudo depmod -a
echo cdc_ncm | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/cdc_ncm.conf
```

Oneshoot that claims the IP and keeps NetworkManager off the iface:

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/usb-ncm-ip.service
[Unit]
Description=Assign IP to Apple USB-C NCM
After=network-pre.target
Wants=network-pre.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'for i in $(seq 1 30); do if ip link show enx52ff74300b99 >/dev/null 2>&1; then nmcli dev set enx52ff74300b99 managed no 2>/dev/null || true; ip addr replace 169.254.67.1/16 dev enx52ff74300b99; ip link set enx52ff74300b99 up; exit 0; fi; sleep 1; done; exit 0'
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now usb-ncm-ip.service
```

## Bring the link up

On the Dell:

```bash
sudo nmcli dev set enx52ff74300b99 managed no
sudo ip link set enx52ff74300b99 up
sudo ip addr replace 169.254.67.1/16 dev enx52ff74300b99
# stop USB autosuspend from killing a long copy
echo on | sudo tee /sys/bus/usb/devices/3-1/power/control
```

On the Mac, `en4` should already be `status: active` and self-assign `169.254.x.x`. Confirm:

```bash
ifconfig en4
ping -c 2 169.254.67.1
ssh dell-usb 'hostname'
```

Do **not** put a scoped IPv6 address (`fe80::…%en4`) in an rsync dest or raw `HostName`. macOS rsync splits on `:`, and OpenSSH treats `%e` as a config token. If you must use IPv6 in `~/.ssh/config`, write `%%en4`.

IPv4 `169.254.67.1` is the reliable target.

## Copy files

Stop any leftover Wi-Fi rsync first so the two copies do not fight.

```bash
# example: Ollama model blobs + manifest
rsync -av --progress --partial --inplace \
  -e ssh \
  ~/.ollama/models/blobs/sha256-<blob> \
  dell-usb:~/.ollama/models/blobs/

rsync -av -e ssh \
  ~/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/<model>/latest \
  dell-usb:~/.ollama/models/manifests/registry.ollama.ai/library/<model>/latest
```

`--partial --inplace` keeps a truncated dest file if SSH drops, so a retry resumes instead of restarting.

Then on the Dell:

```bash
ollama list
```

## What we measured

| Path | Rate | 3.3 GB `gemma3` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Wi-Fi (`10.158.158.1`) | 1–2 MB/s, bursty | hours |
| USB-C NCM (this cable) | **~40 MB/s** steady | **~82 s** |

This cable negotiated **USB 2.0 / 480 Mbps** (`lsusb` Bus 003, Mac `en4` media `100baseTX`). 40 MB/s is about the ceiling for that link.

To go faster, replug onto a SuperSpeed port/cable until `lsusb -t` shows the Mac on a `20000M` bus instead of `480M`. The Dell cannot be a USB gadget (`/sys/class/udc` is empty); Linux stays host, the Mac stays device.

## If the copy dies mid-file

The NCM link can drop under load (`Read from remote host … Operation timed out`). Re-apply the Dell IP, ping `169.254.67.1` from the Mac, then rerun the same `rsync --partial --inplace`. Do not start a second rsync over Wi-Fi at the same time.

Also keep NetworkManager from flushing the USB iface (`nmcli dev set … managed no`). That is why the IPv4 address disappeared once after the first bind.

I'll trace the diligence path — deck extract, Firecrawl, and the model — to see why it's slow and why it comes back wrong.

It is slow because one “due diligence” click is a long serial chain on one GPU, and it looks broken because that chain often fails before it writes anything useful.

**Why it takes so long**

For each named founder we do: Firecrawl search → sometimes a second search → scrape up to two pages → then Muse Glimmer writes a memo. Then we do the same for market (three searches, scrapes, another memo), then portraits. None of that is parallel.

Glimmer is the expensive part. It is an 18GB thinking model. The OpenAI `/v1` call often comes back with empty `content`, so we immediately run the same prompt again on native `/api/chat`. If the JSON is not valid — Glimmer does this a lot — `requireJson` retries **three times**. One founder read can be six full generations. That is what hung the box last time.

Firecrawl adds more wait: 429s retry up to four times, and LinkedIn pages are skipped so we only get thin snippets anyway.

**Why it does not work properly**

The deck already has the facts (Elena Marchetti, Rajesh Anand, Reno, $120B TAM). We do not use that as the memo. We throw those names at the open web, then ask Glimmer to write JSON from scraps. The name parser also ate slide labels (`RA Rajesh Anand`). If JSON fails, the whole founder or market pass is marked skipped. Helion’s research never finished — the job crashed the machine first.

So the UI looks empty or wrong not because diligence “isn’t wired,” but because the live path is **search + thinking-model JSON**, not **deck facts first, public sources only when they land**. That is why a first-pass read feels both slow and incomplete.
